correctness.rationale: The final claim is a finite universal statement over six explicit published facet lists. The standalone verifier checks each is a closed 12-vertex degree-7 triangulated surface, computes mod-two boundary ranks 11 and 27 and therefore H1 dimension 4, exhausts every graph triangle, tests each nonfacial triangle boundary for exact membership in im(partial_2), and groups all nonzero boundaries by exact homology equivalence. Replay returns the claimed count and multiplicity profiles. The nonseparating conclusion uses the standard separating iff mod-two-null criterion for a simple closed curve on a closed orientable surface.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General genus-two map and face-width literature can motivate essential cycles and classify symmetric maps, but the inspected sources do not dominate the exact all-six triangular-homology census. In particular, vertex-transitive coverage applies only to a symmetry-restricted subfamily and does not imply the boundary status or multiplicity profile of every nonfacial triangle.

originality.rationale: The exact-object classification and enumeration sources establish the six complexes, their equivelar character, and symmetry/enumeration facts, but the inspected material does not state or imply that every nonfacial triangle is mod-two essential, nor the six systolic counts or the homology-class multiplicity profiles. published-finding corpus and web searches over exact, equivalent, numerical, and broader formulations found no covering statement. The conclusion is not a formal consequence of degree-regularity or the family count: each boundary-membership decision is independently computed from the exact facet data.

value.rationale: The source literature classifies a complete natural family of equivelar genus-two triangulations. The shortest nonzero homology cycles are an intrinsic combinatorial-systolic layer, and triangular cycles are also the local obstructions relevant to edge contraction and embedding width. Showing that every nonfacial triangle is nonseparating across the entire family, then classifying their exact homology-class multiplicities, gives a structural topological fingerprint rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a known-table recomputation.
